misconception: Compare p=(0.499995,0.00001,0.499995) with qA=(0.9998,0.0001,0.0001) and uniform qB. Which candidate has smaller KL(q||p)? The prediction alternatives contrast different consequences of the stated model.

claims.text: Compare p=(0.499995,0.00001,0.499995) with qA=(0.9998,0.0001,0.0001) and uniform qB. Which candidate has smaller KL(q||p)? Options: qA; qB; They tie. Toy model: compare two controlled cases.
claims.source: Stipulated numerical case in model.ts, based on manager numericCase: Discrete posterior p=[.499995,.00001,.499995]. Candidate mode-hugging qA=[.9998,.0001,.0001], broad qB=[1/3,1/3,1/3]. Compute KL(q||p) and KL(p||q) by finite sums. Reverse KL prefers A; forward KL prefers B. Only these finite candidates are compared, not an asserted universal optimizer.

claims.text: If p assigns positive probability where q is exactly zero, what happens to KL(p||q)? A positive p mass multiplies log(p/0), making the divergence infinite.
